parsed.why: No trans-specific offence or documented visitor-facing restriction; same-sex decriminalised and court-recognised gender change. Hate-crime enforcement gap and thin GI protections, but prosecution reopened. Reduced risk.

Court rulings protect marker change and toilet access, but implementation unclear; no hate-crime or anti-discrimination law; documented toilet abuse and 2013 customs sexual abuse in a small jurisdiction. Elevated.
No criminalisation, but no legal recognition or anti-discrimination; police dismiss trans victims' complaints over male ID, documented impunity and elevated assault; healthcare stigma. Elevated.

State-imposed passport/visa marker restrictions, border refusals and fraud exposure; facility bans with criminal trespass and arrest; hostile custody and counterterror rhetoric, though courts and some protections remain. High risk.
Gender nonconformity itself criminal under uncodified sharia; documented arrests, mass lashing, custody death and deportation; traveller arrested for social posts. Severe, near do-not-visit.
